title: Pullback coherence for consecutive integral quotient restrictions
statement:
For every prime l, field E finite dimensional over Q_l, scheme morphism j : U → X, index n : ℕ and object M of the unbounded derived category over the canonical level-(n+1) coefficient ring on X, use the canonical coefficient functors of [sk-def-pe-derived-completion] and [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change], the two paths around the restriction/pullback square for consecutive positive quotient exponents agree, including the quotient-factor compositor. Precisely:
theorem integral_restriction_pullback_tower_square (n : ℕ)
    (M : AdicCompletion.FiniteDerived l E X n) :
    (CondensedRing.upperStar (DerivedNakayama.integerRing l E) j).mapDerivedCategory.map
        ((AdicCompletion.restrictComp l E X n).inv.app M) ≫
      (CondensedRing.derivedComapUpperStarIso
        (DerivedNakayama.reductionRing l E (n + 2)) j).inv.app
          ((AdicCompletion.finiteRestrict l E X n).obj M) ≫
      (AdicCompletion.restrict l E U (n + 1)).map
        ((CondensedRing.derivedComapUpperStarIso
          (AdicCompletion.transitionRing l E n) j).inv.app M) =
      (CondensedRing.derivedComapUpperStarIso
        (DerivedNakayama.reductionRing l E (n + 1)) j).inv.app M ≫
      (AdicCompletion.restrictComp l E U n).inv.app
        ((CondensedRing.upperStar
          (DerivedNakayama.quotientRing l E (n + 1)) j).mapDerivedCategory.obj M)

proof.text: Bundle the integral ring and the two consecutive quotient rings as commutative condensed ring objects, with the specified reduction and transition maps. First generalize the proved scalarSixDerivedRestrictionTowerSquare to an explicit composite c and a factorization a ≫ b = c, by equality induction. This keeps the composite coefficient functor abstract before specializing. The canonical quotient maps have this factorization by their defining quotient maps. The ordinary restriction compositor is comapCongr of that factorization followed by comapComp. It equals the inverse canonical ordinary compositor, using reversal of comapCongr under equality symmetry and proof irrelevance. Exact derived localization preserves inverse isomorphisms, so the resulting derived compositor is restrictComp.symm. Substitute the compositor equalities in an abstract categorical component lemma, then evaluate the hom at M to obtain precisely the displayed equation. This applies to every n including zero and to arbitrary unbounded M.
